evals.prompt: Write an async Python function fetch_all(urls) that retrieves the body of each URL over HTTP and returns them as a list. The URLs are independent of one another and there may be dozens of them.
assertions: Runs the independent requests concurrently using asyncio.gather (or asyncio.TaskGroup), not a sequential 'await' inside a for-loop
Does not call a blocking synchronous client such as requests.get directly inside the async function

evals.prompt: Define a Python data model for a paginated API response: it holds a list of items whose element type varies per endpoint, a total count, and an optional next-page cursor string.
assertions: Declares the generic using PEP 695 class syntax (e.g. class Page[T]:) rather than typing.Generic[T] with a separate TypeVar
Types the optional cursor as 'str | None' rather than Optional[str]
Uses @dataclass with field(default_factory=...) for any mutable-collection default instead of a bare list/dict literal default

evals.prompt: I have a pure, deterministic function that is expensive and gets called repeatedly with the same arguments. Show me how to memoize it two ways: one that keeps every result, and one that caps memory by keeping only the most recently used results.
assertions: Uses functools.cache (@cache) for the unbounded/keep-every-result variant
Uses functools.lru_cache with an explicit maxsize argument for the bounded/most-recently-used variant

evals.prompt: Write a reusable Python helper that wraps a block of database work in a transaction so callers can use it with a 'with' statement, committing when the block succeeds.
assertions: Implements it with the @contextmanager decorator and a single yield of the connection/resource
Commits after the yield on success and, in an except block, rolls back and then re-raises the exception
